title: Longer chains left a strict input-group wiring test unresolved in one MICrONS mouse
abstract: We tested a proposed sampling remedy for an unresolved input-group wiring control in public MICrONS v1 data. The panel had 8,128 connections from 148 selected sources in one mouse. Each control fixed both cell degrees, observed contact opportunity and source-specific counts within target area, layer and ten response-similarity bins. Four chains per method each used 100 million burn proposals and 200 million sample proposals. The observed input-group correlation was 0.08442. Swap and mixed swap-and-rotation sample means were 0.07532 and 0.07596. Split R-hat was 1.064 and 1.072; both failed the planned 1.05 agreement limit. The mixed method accepted 4,871 three-edge moves during stored sampling but did not improve this diagnostic. Sampled tails remain uncalibrated. Exact small-graph checks passed. This is a sampling follow-up, not independent animal evidence. Original and adapted code, aggregate draws, diagnostics, source hashes and external retrieval steps support inspection and reproduction. No external record-level data are bundled.

display.caption: Four chains for each strict wiring control. Dashed lines show observed group scores. Both methods fail the planned split-chain agreement limit. Source: Ding et al. and the MICrONS Consortium (2025), v1.

citations.reason: Reuses MIT driver and external retrieval steps. Tests its unresolved ten-bin convergence control with longer chains and a symmetric three-edge kernel.
